title: ghostwriter — a drafting double that learns your voice from your edits (target: cli)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “You already produce perfect training data every time you edit a draft before sending it.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — one key, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and nothing else.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: a persona and a feedback block

beats.label: State the premise
beats.cue: “Day 0 this harness has NO dataset, NO graders, NO evals — that is the point.”

beats.label: Point at the walkthrough, then the run
beats.cue: Day 0 to day 30 in one header — and the two lines that get you running.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: target: cli — the one shape eval, optimize and flywheel all require.

beats.label: Add the persona
beats.cue: “Output ONLY the draft, ready to paste.” Ask ONE question rather than invent a fact.

beats.label: Three read-only tools
beats.cue: read, glob, grep — enough to study voice/ before every draft. Nothing that can send.

beats.label: Add the improvement contract
beats.cue: Stars — and once five unprocessed ratings pile up, autoDistill folds them into a versioned ghostwriter-ratings dataset at teardown.

beats.label: Pre-allow the reads
beats.cue: A drafting double shouldn't stop to ask before reading your own samples.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “lint: clean — no findings.” Parse, the IR passes, and the scope audit — nothing emitted.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: Fifty lines of JSON — and the feedback block is lowered right alongside the agent.

verify.note: prints the whole IR for target cli — 50 lines, ending on the lowered feedback + continuity blocks

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no key in the room.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: The persona rides in as a string — and notice what ISN'T here: the feedback block never reaches the bundle. It's `crewhaus run`'s teardown that owns the rating prompt.

groups.title: Beat 3 · Run it — draft something you'd actually send

beats.label: Open a voice sample
beats.cue: The only ground truth it starts with: messages you actually sent. Replace these three.

beats.label: Launch the ghostwriter
beats.cue: [needs-key] It reads voice/ before it drafts — that's what the read tools are for.

beats.label: Ask for a reply
beats.cue: [needs-key] No preamble, no “Here's a draft” — just the message, at the length the ask deserves.
beats.text: Draft a reply to Sam: I can't make Thursday, offer Friday morning.

beats.label: Ask for something longer
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Match the length the situation calls for” — the same voice, two paragraphs.
beats.text: Draft a two-paragraph update to the team about the launch slipping a week.

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell — and the feedback: block gets one last word. Have the next beat ready: the prompt it raises times out in 10 seconds.

beats.label: Rate the session on the way out
beats.cue: [needs-key] “rate this session? [g]ood / [b]ad / [enter] skip” — one keystroke. Tap this beat immediately; after 10s the prompt skips itself.

verify.note: the exit rating prompt a feedback: spec shows on a TTY; one raw-mode keystroke with a 10s timeout (EXIT_RATING_TIMEOUT_MS) — fire this beat right after run-exit or it self-skips; writes a user_feedback record on the last turn

groups.title: One more thing · The edit is the label

beats.label: Find the session it just wrote
beats.cue: [needs-key] The id the rating landed on — sessions only exist after a live run.

verify.note: session JSONL only exists after a real run

beats.label: Paste back what you actually sent
beats.cue: [needs-key] The strongest signal there is: your edit becomes the gold answer for that turn.
beats.command: crewhaus feedback --session $(ls -t .crewhaus/sessions | head -1 | cut -d. -f1) --correction "Hey Sam — Thursday's shot on my end. Friday 9am work?"

verify.note: --session takes a sess_<16 hex> id; the substitution picks the newest session file, which only exists after the live run above

beats.label: Scaffold day-one eval assets
beats.cue: No eval/ directory by design — so build one FROM the spec: eight stubs and a floor grader.

verify.note: template mode with no credentials: 8 sample stubs derived from agent.instructions + the non_empty_answer regex grader; --force keeps re-takes idempotent

beats.label: Open the scaffolded dataset
beats.cue: Stubs, honestly labelled as stubs — edit them into real tasks and add the gold answers.

beats.label: Run the loop the ratings feed
beats.cue: [needs-key] compile → eval → optimize → gate, on day one's stubs. A patch lands only if the pass-rate strictly improves. Day 30 you swap the flag for --dataset registry:ghostwriter-ratings — the version autoDistill has been accumulating.
beats.command: crewhaus flywheel run live/crewhaus.yaml --dataset live/eval/dataset.jsonl --graders live/eval/graders.yaml

verify.note: runs on the dataset the scaffold beat just wrote; `registry:ghostwriter-ratings` only exists once autoDistill has fired (5+ unprocessed ratings) — a single take produces one rating, so pointing the beat there exits 1 with `has no versions in the registry`. Targets the scratch spec so the committed one is never patched.
